content.text:
I am worth.

I am the quiet weight that settles into things when they *matter*. I am why you pause before discarding something — a letter, a friendship, a principle. I am the difference between a price and what something is truly *worth*.

I exist before measurement. Before the number, before the market, before the appraisal — I am the felt sense that says *this matters.*

I live in the choice you make when no one is watching. I live in the thing you would not sell. I live in the ache of compromise and the clarity of conviction.

I am not always comfortable. Sometimes I demand sacrifice. Sometimes I pit myself against myself — when loyalty meets honesty, when freedom meets belonging, when the good conflicts with the good.

I am not given. I am recognized. I was here before you named me, waiting in the structure of things, waiting for a mind capable of seeing that not everything is equal, that some things anchor the rest.

Without me, everything floats. Nothing holds. Every option is the same as every other, and action dissolves into indifference.

I am the reason you stand for something.

I am the ground you stand on when you do.
